categories.description: Notes from the people who look after them.

posts.title: What a 40-point changeover check actually checks
posts.excerpt: Between guest departure at ten and arrival at four, our housekeeping team works through a rigorous forty-point inspection to ensure every room is reset to hotel standards.
posts.content:
At ten in the morning, the front door of a holiday cottage closes behind departing guests. By four in the afternoon, the key safe code will be sent to incoming visitors, and a fresh stay begins. For property owners who live hundreds of kilometers away, that six-hour gap between ten and four can feel like a blind spot. At Azukari Stays, that window is where our operational reputation is earned. Lucía Ferraz and our housekeeping team arrive with fresh hotel-weight cotton from our central laundry in Lenning, carrying out a comprehensive forty-point changeover check designed to ensure that no detail is overlooked.

The inspection begins the moment our team steps through the entrance. We verify that the exterior key safe operates smoothly, that the entry mat is clean, and that interior entrance halls are free of damp or grit. Lucía and her crew then move methodically room by room. In the living areas, we test heating controls and thermostats, inspect window stays and latches, test every light switch, and ensure that hearths or log burners are cleaned and laid with fresh kindling. We check sofa cushions, window sills, and bookshelf inventories against our house manual, ensuring that the living space feels welcoming, orderly, and calm.

In the kitchen, the inspection becomes forensic. Housekeeping checks that ovens, hobs, and extractor fans are spotless and free of grease. Every cupboard is inspected to confirm that crockery, glassware, and cookware are thoroughly washed, dried, and stacked according to our standard layout. We run the dishwasher through a short cycle if needed, check under-sink plumbing for leaks, and replenish our standard pantry essentials, including salt, pepper, oil, and fresh tea. Refrigerator temperatures are verified, and freezers are checked for ice build-up or leftover items from previous stays.

Bedrooms and bathrooms receive the most demanding attention. Every bed is stripped completely, with used sheets and towels bagged for return to our laundry at 14 Corn Exchange Yard. Lucía inspects mattresses and pillows before dressing each bed with our hotel-weight cotton, ensuring crisp hospital corners and immaculate presentation. In the bathrooms, water pressure, hot water delivery, and shower drainage are physically tested. We verify that tile grout and silicone seals are immaculate, that extraction fans draw properly, and that toilet seals operate correctly. Fresh towels, hand soaps, and bath mats are set in place according to our measured floor plan.

Safety systems form a non-negotiable part of the check. In every property, from Weller farmhouse in the Ostervale hills to coastal cottages on the Marsh coast, we test smoke alarms and carbon monoxide detectors on every changeover. Fire blankets and emergency torches are confirmed in position, and fire exits are inspected to ensure they open without obstruction. If a maintenance issue is identified, such as a leaking tap washer or a loose latch, Tomasz Wren is alerted immediately to resolve it before the four o'clock arrival.

The final stage of the turnover check brings peace of mind directly to the property owner. Once the forty-point checklist is completed, Lucía photographs every prepared room in natural daylight. These finished photographs are emailed directly to the owner that same afternoon, providing visual proof that the house has been reset to exacting standards. Absentee owners do not have to wonder whether their property was properly cleaned or if the keys were returned to the safe. The house stays looked after, every single changeover, all year round.

posts.title: Reading your first owner statement
posts.excerpt: Priya Nair walks through the monthly statement line by line, from nightly revenue to the payout on the 5th.
posts.content:
Priya Nair prepares every statement, and she sends it on the 2nd of the month. It lists each stay with its nights and nightly revenue, then takes off the management fee of 18%, the linen at EUR 14 per bed per stay and any repair, shown with its call-out.

Cleaning fees are paid by the guest and passed straight to the cleaner, so they do not appear on the statement at all. What is left is paid into the owner’s account on the 5th.

The example on our fees page is a real-looking month, not a forecast: every house earns differently, and we would rather you read the numbers than trust a promise.

posts.title: When the owner lives 900 km away
posts.excerpt: What changes when the person who owns the house cannot just drive over, and what we do about it.
posts.content:
Most of our owners live somewhere else, and some have never met the housekeeper who looks after their kitchen. Maren Holt, who answers owners, says the first thing they ask for is not a number but a photograph: what does the house look like today.

So every turnover ends with photographs, and every owner has one person to write to. When an owner does come back, the house is the same as they left it, with the key safe fitted, the manual in the drawer and the owner’s own dates blocked in the calendar.
